## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Verify the wheel has a 6x5.5 inch bolt pattern.
2. Confirm the center hole is larger than the vehicle's hub bore (106mm for Toyota vs 100mm on Nissan/Frontier).
3. Select one of four mounting methods: steel wheels with factory hubs, swapped wheel studs, bolt-on spacers, or mag-shank lug nuts.
4. If using a spacer larger than the front hub material allows (e.g., SpiderTrax), switch to KSP style over-hub spacers.

_Procedure reported by [t1210]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1424] [Partial]</summary>

1. Trim the front fenders back to where they meet the cab corners.
2. Hammer or flatten the pinch seam on the front quarter panels using a ball peen hammer (BFH).
3. Raise the inner shield that covers the fuel lines if it interferes with tire clearance.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1424] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Cut back to the cab corner at the bottom of the front fender.
2. Beat the pinch seam in the fender well flat with a ball peen hammer (BFH).
3. [Partial] Move the passenger side shield up by a couple inches.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1194] [Partial]</summary>

1. Adjust the front torsion bar to level a side that rides lower than its counterpart.
2. Mark the plastic trim on both front wheel wells with tape.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1194] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Mount the tire on a wheel with 5-inch backspace.
2. [Partial] Install extended thread (ET) style lug nuts to fit over factory studs.

</details>

## Parts

- 1/4 inch male to male connector [t1699]
- [Partial] 106mm to 100mm Hub Rings: Required for aluminum wheels or when using factory Nissan studs; may need centering care on steel wheels. [t1210]
- 3/8 inch inner diameter hose, approx. 3ft [t1699]
- 6 x 5.5 inch, or 139.7 mm lug pattern wheel [t1196]
- [Partial] Blank Hub Caps: Optional plastic caps without brand logos to hide the center of a mismatched wheel. [t1210]
- Bolt-on Wheel Spacers: KSP style recommended for over-hub fitment on front; 1 inch width suggested to manage offset. [t1210]
- General Grabber, not AT2 [t1195]
- Goodyear MT/R w/Kevlar [t1195]
- Mag Shank Lug Nuts, M12 x 1.25: Designed to fit Nissan studs while centering a Toyota wheel; shank diameter must match the mag nut. [t1210]
- Mag Shank Lug Nuts, M12 x 1.5: Knurl diameter approx 0.506-.509 inches; under-head length roughly 1.5in to press into rear hub. [t1210]
- Pressure gauge with ball valve [t1699]
- Small hose clamps [t1699]
- Tire valve chuck with clip [t1699]
- Wheel with center bore of at least 100mm [t1196]
- [Partial] Yokohama Geolandar I/T [t1195]
- Yokohama Geolandar I/T, Winter Tire [t1195]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Extends ground clearance by moving weight lower or adds utility storage. [t1045]
- Expect road noise to increase with aggressive off-road tires, but accept it for better performance. [t1195]
- Note that Goodyear MT/R Kevlars can become hard to balance as they wear unevenly. [t1195]
- [Unverified value] These tires perform well at low pressures (12-14 psi) for rock crawling. [t1195]
- [Partial] They are heavy and generate noticeable highway noise, but offer superior traction over BFGoodrich or Duratracs. [t1195]
- [Partial] They are light on the road with minimal noise compared to aggressive mud tires. [t1195]
- These tires offer decent rain traction but may struggle in deep snow or mud without pressure reduction. [t1195]
- They are described as having 'nice on the road' characteristics despite being aggressive. [t1195]
- Look for wheels from Chevrolet, Dodge, Hummer, Isuzu, Mazda, Mitsubishi, Nissan, Suzuki, or Infiniti manufactured in the years listed below. [t1196]
- [Partial] Note that some Chevy and Toyota wheels are hub-centric with a flat flange on lug nuts rather than a taper, which may affect seating. [t1196]
- A 2-inch body lift provides clearance for wider tires than a PML kit. [t1641]
- Note that 33x12.50 tires work well with a PML, 2-inch body lift, and minor trimming. [t1649]
- Wider wheels (8-10 inches) allow the tire to sit wider than narrower ones. [t1649]
- Use a Thor hammer for pounding out tight spots without over-trimming. [t1649]
- Expect rubbing on the lower control arms at full lock when combining this setup with a PML and 2-inch body lift. [t1649]
- Verify no abnormal wear occurs after installation. [t1649]
- Ensure the valve chuck has a clip so it stays connected. [t1699]
- Use pipe tape if the connectors do not have pre-applied compound. [t1699]
- Stand up while operating rather than crouching next to the tire. [t1699]
- [Partial] Consider wheel size and tree branches when choosing between spring mounts or rigid whips. [t2332]
- [Partial] A longer whip provides better reception in open areas but may require more clearance. [t2332]
- [Partial] Extend rear bump stops to gain extra wheel travel without cutting the rear fenders. [t1424]
- Tighten lug nuts in a star pattern slightly at a time when using hub rings with steel wheels. [t1210]
- Consider BFGoodrich KM2s in size 33x10.50-15R or Kumho Mud Terrain tires as popular choices. [t1834]
- Interco Tires are noted for being purpose-specific, ideal for dedicated crawlers, mudders, or desert runners. [t1834]
- Michelin LTX A/T2 in size 31x10.50-15 is suggested for less rolling resistance and longevity. [t1834]
- [Partial] General Tire DuraTracs are recommended as a balance between street manners and off-road capability. [t1834]
- Cooper Discoverer STT is recommended for off-road trails and mud but may require frequent rotation to maintain even road wear. [t1834]
- Toyo Open Country M/Ts are suggested specifically for non-sand trail, mud, and daily driving. [t1834]
- Kenda Klever M/T is noted as an affordable option with good reviews, though some question its Chinese manufacturing origin. [t1834]
- GT Radial Adventuro M/T provides winter weather capability but may have noticeable road noise compared to all-terrains. [t1834]
- Pro Comp Xtreme Mud-Terrains are suggested as having killer performance and good road manners, though availability is limited to 16-inch wheels or larger. [t1834]
- General Tire Red Label Trep is suggested specifically for sandy conditions. [t1834]
- [Partial] BFGoodrich All-Terrain tires are frequently mentioned as a reliable standard choice that balances price and performance. [t1834]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Assuming all 6 x 5.5 pattern wheels will seat perfectly without checking the center bore or lug nut design (flat vs tapered). [t1196]
- [Partial] Cutting too much into the front quarter panel back side, extending all the way to the doors (though this may be necessary for wider tires). [t1424]
- [Partial] Using regular acorn seat lug nuts (Nissan style) directly on aluminum Toyota wheels without mag shanks, risking the wheel falling off. [t1210]
- [Partial] Choosing SpiderTrax spacers for front hubs where material thickness prevents fitment over the hub. [t1210]
- [Partial] Running tires that wear too fast on the road if budget allows for better options. [t1834]
- Experiencing rough road manners with the Cooper STT if not rotated often. [t1834]
- Dealing with potential sidewall blowouts on BFGoodrich models if running over rocks frequently. [t1834]
- [Partial] Finding the specific tire size difficult if not running a standard wheel width. [t1834]
